questions.explanation: Part 5, Steps 2 and 4: ip and ping cover networking, apt-get/apt-cache manage packages, and speedtest-cli is the example package installed and used.

questions.text: Adding -l to ls changes the output to include which of these?
options: Permissions, owner, group, size and modification date for each item
A count of files only, no names
questions.explanation: Part 2, Step 2c: the "long display" adds all of these columns that plain ls leaves out.

questions.text: -l and -r can be combined into a single -lr flag on the same ls call.
questions.explanation: True — Part 2, Step 2e: "Multiple options can be used at the same time," demonstrated with ls -lr.

questions.text: Fill in the flag that grants execute permission on a file with chmod.
questions.explanation: Part 3, Step 2f. Without it, the permission string has no x and the file can't be run.

questions.text: In sudo chown root myfile.sh, what does the argument root specify?
options: The directory to move the file into
The new owning user for the file
The new owning group for the file
questions.explanation: Part 3, Step 2h-i. chown's bare argument (no group after a colon) only changes the owning user.

questions.text: Which of these three gives the most detailed listing of every running process on the machine?
questions.explanation: Part 5, Step 3: plain ps is limited to the current terminal, -e adds every process on the system, and -ef adds full columns like UID and PPID on top of that.

questions.text: Fill in the option that limits ping to a fixed number of packets instead of running forever.
questions.explanation: Part 5, Step 2b: -c 4 capped the ping at four packets.

questions.text: What does passwd -S do, compared to plain passwd?
options: It reports the password's current status instead of changing it
It forces an immediate password change
questions.explanation: Part 5, Step 5a-b: plain passwd updates the password; -S only reports on its status.

options: Cancels a shutdown that was already scheduled
Schedules a new shutdown one minute out
questions.explanation: Part 5, Step 1c: after scheduling shutdown +1 "Come back soon!", the lab has you cancel it with shutdown -c.

questions.text: apt-cache search does not require sudo, unlike apt-get update, install, upgrade or purge.
questions.explanation: True — Part 5, Step 4b runs apt-cache search speed test with no sudo, since it only reads the local cache rather than changing the system.

questions.text: In sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli, what does the argument speedtest-cli specify?
options: The exact name of the package to download and install
A search keyword to look for a package
questions.explanation: Part 5, Step 4c. Unlike apt-cache search, which takes a loose keyword, apt-get install needs the package's exact name.

questions.text: Fill in the anchor character that makes grep match only lines starting with the given text.
questions.explanation: Part 4c. grep's pattern argument can include regex anchors like ^ and $, not just literal text.

questions.text: In :w linux3.txt inside vi, what does the argument linux3.txt do?
options: Names the file the current buffer should be saved to
Names a file to open next
questions.explanation: Part 3, Step 7c: :w normally saves under the file's current name, but giving it an argument saves to that name instead — which is how linux2.txt's edits ended up in a new file, linux3.txt.

questions.text: In cd Documents, is Documents an option or an argument?
options: An argument — it names the specific target the command acts on
An option — it modifies how cd behaves
Neither — it's part of the command name itself
questions.explanation: Options are flags that start with a dash (like -l); Documents has no dash, so it's the argument — the specific thing cd is told to act on.

questions.text: man and --help both take the target command's name as their argument.
questions.explanation: True — man ls and ls --help both name ls as their target, though --help is attached to the command itself as a flag rather than passed to a separate program.
